kept.spine: Nothing tests Rundgate at present, and that is not chance. A town kept this ready is not worth the cost of trying.
What comes out of the country beyond the frontier is known here, and nobody raises it above a mutter. The town takes the silence itself as a sign the arrangement is holding.
faces: A traveller says the road warns a man of what is out there long before the gate does.
The men who hold the ways in drop the bar at dusk, and no one argues the hour with them.
A priest of one of the parishes prays for the men who stand the line in the same breath as the roads.
One of the aldermen holds that nothing about the nights beyond the wall has reached the hall as a complaint.
A night patrolman says whatever comes in from the country stops at the gate and goes no further as talk.
At the long table a woman says the drink is for the ones who stand the nights, and the country past the wall never comes up.
A soldier of the garrison points out that no one from the town turns out to watch a drill.
A guild factor reckons the trades pay the toll on the way through, and count the line it buys as everyone's.
A stallholder says the stalls go up the same whatever the country beyond is doing.
A clerk of the court says a dispute over the toll on the way through is settled the day it is brought, and the country brings it none.
The elders say the young stand the nights and the old say how they are stood.

kept.poolKey: Invasion & War: walls AND professional garrison
kept.spine: A traveller is stopped at the gate and counted before he is waved through. What he steps into afterward is a town that keeps its own soldiers under pay.
faces: A gatekeeper says the toll a stranger pays at the gate reaches the hall only when the gate gets round to it.
A woman who keeps the hall books says a stranger who has paid at the gate has paid the town in full, whatever the gatekeeper tells him.
A bailiff holds that anyone who paid the toll may argue the sum before the court, a stranger the same as a carter.
A pedlar says his pack was opened at the gate and nothing came out of it but the toll.
At the tavern an innkeeper says the town was never asked whether it wanted soldiers of its own, only what they cost.

kept.spine: A court sits at Rundgate, and no room in the town holds a man overnight. The law here is left with two things to take, a man's coin or his place among his neighbours.
faces: One of the watch says whatever it takes up after dark is settled after dark, there being no room to keep a man until the morning.
The officers of the court say they hear by daylight what the watch already settled in the dark, and nobody consults them first.
A clerk in the hall reckons the purse has never run to a cell, and does not say who first asked for one.
At the market a stallholder says a short weight goes before a magistrate and comes back as a sum. The scales it was weighed on stay on his stall.
A priest of one of the parishes holds that the parish keeps a place for a man once he is dead, and the town keeps none for him while he lives.
A guild factor reckons a sum is taken from a man's earnings and forgotten, and the mark it leaves on his work is not.
A man who drinks where the carters drink says a man with a house here pays and stays, and a man without one is told to go.
A drover notes there is nothing here to take from a man who owns nothing in the town, so the town has only the one thing left to do with him.
A man on one of the gates says they are handed a man and a direction, and given no reason for either.
A serjeant of the garrison says what comes for the town is the garrison's business, and the people put out of it are not.

kept.spine: Everyone in the town has watched the grain store kept full, and takes that as proof that a hard season would find the place provided for.
faces: The mayor says the hall asks the trades for no more than the trades can bear.
The guilds of the town say the carrying of it is theirs, and the asking of it is not.
Of the two, the guilds have the likelier account, the hall having a purse of its own to defend and the guilds only a bill to point to.
One of the watch holds that the rounds are kept by men who are owed pay for keeping them.
Whoever keeps the toll book says a cart headed for the grain store never waits at the gate, no matter what else does.
A rider who stopped a night says he heard the grain store praised and the garrison's wage complained of, from the same mouths.
The drinkers of the district hold that the watch is a trade that drinks on what it is owed.
The garrison reckons that a town able to feed itself through a bad season and still short its wage has decided something, without saying what.
The traders at the fair say the stallholders settle what the hall is owed before they settle anything of their own.
A priest of one of the parishes holds that the town keeps its word to the dead sooner than it keeps its word to the living.

kept.spine: A working balance holds at Rundgate. The law stands, crime exists, and neither one has the run of the town.

kept.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
kept.spine: The safety reading for Rundgate is a first one. It is plain about what has been seen and silent about what has not.
A stranger at Rundgate is not robbed, only quietly told what the arrangement is, and the danger here is a matter of system, not of surprise.
The walls at Rundgate hold its entry points under one control. That is what a perimeter buys, not safety outright but the choice of where trouble happens.
Rundgate keeps a standing force, men whose work is the defense of the town and who answer for it as work, not as duty owed.
The town pays for a portion of its soldiers outright and keeps a clear account of which ones those are.
A stranger at Rundgate finds a hall whose business is trouble no garrison is built to handle, and finds the hall doing steady trade.
At the gate a stranger is measured by some means he cannot name, and nobody offers him a reason for it.

The city walls and gates at Rundgate hold up better than the watch meant to stand them. Upkeep for the work runs close to its limit, close enough that the wage side of the defense is the part falling behind.

kept.poolKey: Logistics & Supply: Granary with road supply
kept.spine: Grain is kept in store at Rundgate, and everything else that feeds the town comes in by road, there being no port to share the load. The roads are the town's weak side, and the grain store buys it time to answer for that.
